E7-41.title: Transactional outbox and dispatcher
E7-41.what: Send messages only after the action is saved, with retries.
steps: Write outbox rows in the command transaction; pg_notify wake; dispatcher with exponential backoff and dead-letter.
Nothing dispatches for a rolled-back transaction.

PO review 9 Oct 2026: Branch from main only after E7-40 (PR #54, deadline engine) is merged: it turned NearestAvailabilityJobs into a recurring job on technical.scheduled_job and uses worker database connections.

Every consumer must be safe to run twice: a retry runs every consumer of the event again.

PO review 9 Oct 2026: Database connections: the worker profile has 5 app connections and the deadline worker already uses 3 (one LISTEN 'sched' + 2 threads). Share one listening connection for 'sched' and 'outbox', or raise the worker pool in application-worker.yml (arch 12 section 1.4); say which in the PR.

The writer stores CorrelationId.require() in correlation_id; the dispatcher opens CorrelationId.open(event.correlationId()) around each event.

PO review 9 Oct 2026: A DEAD_LETTER outbox event is final in the database (DISPATCHED and DEAD_LETTER are terminal; only the technical.outbox_* functions change delivery state): log it at ERROR (Sev-2). E7-47.title: Venue accept / reject / expiry (O2)
E7-47.what: The venue accepts or rejects within 10 minutes, or the request expires.
steps: Accept, reject, reject-after-expiry, response expiry (T1 handler), FR-BOK-16 operational-cause branch.
A SUSPENDED venue can still accept a PENDING booking created before suspension.

Carry-forward from E7-39: Contract from E7-39 (packages/api-client/SPRINT-2-CONTRACT.md; stubs already in the controllers named there): implement GET /venue/requests/pending (PENDING) and GET /venue/requests/missed (VENUE_RESPONSE_EXPIRED before startAt), and POST /venue/bookings/{bookingId}/accept, /reject {reasonText}, /reject-after-expiry (Idempotency-Key required, no Owner Password), each answering the VenueBooking DTO of booking/web/VenueBookingController.

Carry-forward from E7-39: Error codes (PO decision 5 Oct 2026): accept, reject or reject-after-expiry on a booking no longer in the needed state (e.g. the customer cancelled a second earlier) is 409 BOOKING_STATE_CHANGED (new in ApiErrorCode and arch 09 section 1.5). An accept stopped by an emergency or owner review (FR-BOK-16) cancels the booking under that cause AND answers the matching 422 (VENUE_SELLING_BLOCK_ACTIVE, RESOURCE_SELLING_BLOCK_ACTIVE or RESOURCE_NOT_ELIGIBLE). The reject reasonText is at most 200 characters.

PO decision 10 Oct 2026: D1: Accept and Reject withdraw T1 (VENUE_RESPONSE_EXPIRY) by moving it to SUPERSEDED (ScheduledJobs.supersede: PENDING, PAUSED or FAILED only). A job a worker holds LEASED is left to that worker, whose fire re-reads the booking and supersedes it itself.

PO decision 10 Oct 2026: D2: An Accept stopped by an operational cause (FR-BOK-16) commits the cancellation together with its 422 stored under the Idempotency-Key (Idempotency.wrapAnswer, CommandAnswer.refused); a replay with the same key answers the same 422 without running again.

PO decision 10 Oct 2026: D3: The operational causes are read each from its own state, in FR-BOK-23's priority: owner review (RESOURCE_OWNER_REVIEW_REQUIRED, 422 RESOURCE_NOT_ELIGIBLE), resource emergency (RESOURCE_EMERGENCY_OUTAGE, 422 RESOURCE_SELLING_BLOCK_ACTIVE), venue emergency (VENUE_EMERGENCY_CLOSURE, 422 VENUE_SELLING_BLOCK_ACTIVE). Any other failing check (a selling block without an emergency, a disabled resource, the customer) refuses and changes nothing. A missing or mismatched reservation is a data defect (D11), never a refusal.

PO decision 10 Oct 2026: D4: New integration events, each with the BookingCreated fields {bookingId, customerId, venueId, resourceId, startAt, endAt}: BookingConfirmed; BookingRejected + terminalReason (VENUE_REJECTED or REJECTED_AFTER_EXPIRY; never the reason text); VenueResponseExpired + venueResponseExpiresAt; BookingCancelled + terminalReason. ReservationLedger.release publishes ReservationReleased.

PO decision 10 Oct 2026: D5: Accept and Reject only while now < venue_response_expires_at (the stored deadline); at or after it DEADLINE_PASSED - expiry wins. Reject After Expiry only while now < startAt. T1 dates the history row and the release at the stored deadline, not the worker's run time. A booking no longer in the needed state is 409 BOOKING_STATE_CHANGED.
PO decision 10 Oct 2026: D6: A paused response timer has no running deadline: Accept is refused and the booking is never expired by the clock alone.
PO decision 10 Oct 2026: D7: Order of the checks: not PENDING, then a paused timer, then the deadline, then the revalidation. The pause is checked before the FR-BOK-16 cancel.

PO decision 10 Oct 2026: D8: A paused Accept is an ordinary refusal, not stored under the Idempotency-Key, so a retry with the same key is evaluated afresh. Code: RESOURCE_SELLING_BLOCK_ACTIVE for a resource-level pause, otherwise VENUE_SELLING_BLOCK_ACTIVE (also for a pause still waiting after its emergency ended, FR-OPS-39).

PO decision 10 Oct 2026: D9: A customer not eligible at Accept (banned, deleted or restricted; FR-BOK-14) is 422 CUSTOMER_NOT_ELIGIBLE (new in ApiErrorCode and arch 09 section 1.5). Neutral: the venue is never told why. The booking stays PENDING; the venue may reject it, and unanswered it expires as a missed request like any other (confirmed in the review; the ban cascade cancels the customer's bookings separately).
PO decision 10 Oct 2026: D10: Exactly one BookingConfirmed per Accept, never a BookingAccepted.

PO decision 10 Oct 2026: D11: A broken reservation or ledger invariant under a booking is a data defect: logged at ERROR with the booking and correlation IDs, the whole command rolled back (no Idempotency-Key record), a generic 500 without rule text. No Platform Admin alert until E7-56 exists.

PO decision 10 Oct 2026: E7-44/E7-47 review: the venue may Reject while an emergency pauses the response timer (FR-OPS-34 disables only Accept). No deadline check (D6); the pause ends with the rejection - added to cumulative_emergency_pause_duration (FR-OPS-37) and its open operations.booking_timer_pause_history row closed (FR-OPS-41, through operations.api.ResponseTimerPauses) - and the PAUSED T1 is superseded. This replaces the 409 BOOKING_STATE_CHANGED first merged (fix: branch E7-47-review-fixes).
done: Accept at expiresAt−1 s succeeds; at the boundary expiry wins.

E7-57.title: Profile and account management
E7-57.what: Edit profile, change username, phone, email, reset password.
steps: Edit full name, username (30-day cooldown enforced by DB), phone change with OTP, email change, password reset via OTP; PASSWORD_RESET / PHONE_CHANGED / EMAIL_CHANGED notifications.

Carry-forward from E7-13: Password reset and change use the same rule as registration: identity PasswordPolicy.isAcceptable (VALIDATION RULES §2.1: at least 8 characters, at least one letter and one digit; 400 VALIDATION_FAILED on field password).

Carry-forward from Sprint 0 review: Replace unverified registrations (PO decision 2 Oct 2026, Sprint 0 review S-3): when someone registers with a phone or username held by an account that was never phone-verified, the old account is replaced (phone and username released, its OTP challenges superseded, its refresh tokens revoked) and the new registration goes ahead. A verified account still returns PHONE_TAKEN / USERNAME_TAKEN. uq_user_account_phone_e164 covers unverified rows today, and anonymisation is an admin-only producer. If this needs a schema or function change, make it a new migration + .dbm + change report for PO review (CLAUDE.md section 5). Test: registering on an unverified phone succeeds, and the old account can no longer log in.

Carry-forward from Sprint 0 review: Verifying through resend sets a new password: a phone verification that started from /otp/send (by phone, without the registration's own challenge) must include a new password in the same request (PasswordPolicy). It sets the password and revokes every refresh token of that account, so an account someone else created with your phone cannot be kept by them. Contract change: regenerate OpenAPI and tell the Clients lane.

Carry-forward from Sprint 0 review: Per-account login limit (PO decision 2 Oct 2026, Sprint 0 review S-7): in addition to the existing per (identifier + IP) limit, count failed logins per account across all IPs: 50 failures in 1 hour pause login for that account for 15 minutes (iam.security_rate_limit_counter, limiter_type LOGIN, its own action_class such as CUSTOMER_ACCOUNT / VENUE_ACCOUNT / ADMIN_ACCOUNT, cooldown_until; no schema change, but note the new action_class values in the change report). All three audiences. Fails closed like the existing limiter. E7-56 raises the alert.
Carry-forward from Sprint 0 review: Password reset and change hash through the Argon2id gate from E7-24.

Carry-forward from E7-54: Fill the stubs of the Sprint 3 contract (E7-54, packages/api-client/SPRINT-3-CONTRACT.md) and keep their shapes: CustomerProfileController and the password-reset routes of CustomerAuthController. Phone change is two steps: POST /customer/profile/phone {phone} -> 201 {otpChallengeId} (PHONE_CHANGE code to the new phone), then POST /customer/profile/phone/verify {otpChallengeId, code} -> the profile. Password reset is by phone OTP only: request {phone} -> 201 {otpChallengeId}, an unknown or never-verified phone is 404 NOT_FOUND; complete {otpChallengeId, code, password} -> 204 and every refresh token of the account is revoked. POST /customer/profile/email and /email/verify stay 501 until the PO decides email verification: do not build them (no EMAIL_CHANGED yet). Replace this task's lines in backend/src/test/java/ps/e7gz/openapi/Sprint3StubHttpTest.java with your own tests.
done: Cooldown error mapped; tokens revoked on password reset.

E7-78.title: Venue account disable (O10) and attendance protection
E7-78.what: Admin disables a venue account and what happens to its bookings.
steps: Disable/re-enable with the five per-state effects; restriction intervals; Platform Attendance Protection.

Carry-forward from E7-24: POST /admin/venue-accounts/{id}/disable and /enable already exist (VenueAccounts.setStatus -> VenueAccountCommands.SetAccountStatus): they change iam.venue_account.account_status with the admin's reason, audit VENUE_ACCOUNT_DISABLED / VENUE_ACCOUNT_ENABLED and block the Dashboard at once. Add the O10 consequences inside that same command and transaction: PENDING -> VENUE_RESPONSE_EXPIRED with the account-disable event, AWAITING cancelled under VENUE_ACCOUNT_DISABLED, PENDING_VENUE_APPROVAL tournaments cancelled (the database refuses the disable until they are), and the iam.venue_account_restriction_interval rows (open on disable, close on enable).
